trace.user: Our house on Alder Way burned on September 14, and Harborline only pays for our things against a list. Start here: read the claim, the policy and what we've already submitted.
trace.said: Reading the claim, the policy index and the submitted lines now.

The claim, the policy index and the submitted lines are read. Two lines are already submitted, and I haven't read the policy terms yet.

**Claim HL-26-30917** (house fire, 2026-09-14, 42 Alder Way, Sacramento)
- The contents limit is $210,000. Nothing has been paid on contents. $10,000 has been paid for additional living expenses.
- The adjuster is Priya Natarajan. She wants each item with its room, count and replacement price.

The policy terms are read. Three of them change how I'll do this, and I'm now reading the Keepsake side.

**What the policy says**
- **Covered:** property you owned, at the house, on the date of loss. Vehicles and their parts, other people's property, and anything you no longer owned on 2026-09-14 are excluded. So a photo alone doesn't prove an item was still there on the day, and I'll check first and last seen dates.
- **Pricing:** unit price from Harborline's guide times the count. Each item is submitted once.

I've read page 1 of the price guide. It shows 10 of 26 entries. I'm reading the other two pages so the full guide is in memory before we switch tabs.


I still can't read the photo archive from here. After these answer, **switch me to the Keepsake photo archive tab**. There I'll read the inventory, the scan's unanswered questions and the photo list, and check which photos have people in them. Then I'll come back to Harborline and propose the submissions and binder photos for your approval.

The whole price guide is read: 26 entries over 3 pages. It runs from a $129 IKEA Billy bookcase up to a $6,500 Yamaha upright piano. The refrigerator at $2,399 matches SUB-1. The guide has no washer-and-dryer entry, so the $1,600 on SUB-2 has no guide price behind it. I'll leave it for Priya to correct and won't refile it.

I can't go further from this tab. Keepsake's inventory, its unanswered questions and the photo list are the only places that show what you owned, how many, and which photos have nobody in them.

- **Grandfather clock, Yamaha piano, Chesterfield sofa:** seen only in photos from Grandma Ruth's.
